book.title: Daughters of Babylon
book.subtitle: A lyrical archival mystery across centuries
book.description: When Silvina is named executor of her mentor Vivian Lansdowne’s estate, she expects paperwork, not a trail of poems, journals, and artifacts that feel like they are still speaking. As she follows Vivian’s clues toward a ruined priory in southern France, another life presses close: Eleanor of Aquitaine, confined by power and politics, fighting to preserve what history would rather bury, including desire, voice, and names. And in 1972 Veracruz, Lupo Sánchez, a nagual bound to ritual duty, carries visions that read less like dreams than instructions. Thread by thread, manuscripts surface, legends sharpen, and the line between scholarship and the uncanny thins, turning grief into a pursuit and poetry into evidence.

audienceMatch.title: Audience Match
audienceMatch.keyCharacteristics: This is built for upmarket adult readers who like literary prose, layered timelines, and the satisfaction of discovery through found texts, archives, translation, and place rich history. The core audience skews 28 to 55, college educated to postgraduate, with strong book club energy and a preference for indie discovery routes such as staff picks, literary podcasts, festivals, and longform criticism. They tend to value emotional intelligence and thematic depth, and they respond well to a clear organizing hook like an archival mystery while also appreciating multilingual texture, ritual and folklore handled with care, and women centered stakes around agency, legacy, and what survives.

analysisOverview.title: Analysis Overview
analysisOverview.classification: Position this as upmarket literary historical fiction at the intersection of archival mystery and folkloric magical realism: the engine is an investigation powered by poems, manuscripts, and scholarship rather than thriller pace, with atmosphere, sensuality, and intellectual curiosity doing much of the propulsion. It sits naturally alongside readers of archive driven literary mysteries and research forward historical fiction, while also offering a distinctive cross cultural braid through the Veracruz ritual strand and mythic logic. Genre signals in the report are organized using a bespoke taxonomy of subgenres, which helps communicate the book’s thematic and stylistic pull without forcing it into a single shelf, and supports pitching it as a discussion rich, premium literary read.
analysisOverview.personas: The primary reader persona is Maya Rutherford, an upmarket literary “time slip sleuth” who loves dual timelines, found documents, embedded poetry, and psychologically true explorations of grief and cultural memory. She reveals the heart of the readership: people who want beautiful sentences and symbolic, grounded uncanny elements, and who enjoy mapping patterns across time as a form of meaning making. A strong secondary persona is Javier Morales, a bilingual, culturally engaged reader drawn to ritual, folklore, and post colonial identity handled with respect, which signals meaningful crossover potential among readers who want spiritual specificity and emotional stakes rather than spectacle.
analysisOverview.marketingGuidance: Use the insights here to shape early campaigns around the most legible hooks, then deepen with craft and atmosphere: a mentor’s estate that becomes an archive, a queen in captivity preserving a voice, a nagual carrying visions, and a ruined priory where poems become proof. Lead with clear promise lines for discovery and conversion, then rotate more lyrical creative for high intent readers who share excerpts and join book club conversations; the report also provides ready to use copy such as blurbs, subject lines, CTAs, and short trailer scripts you can adapt into ads and social assets. These marketing components will expand into a dedicated product over time, but right now they are included as part of the first report so the report holder can launch initial testing with coherent messaging and strong creative angles.

positioning.title: Category Positioning
positioning.subtitle: Upmarket literary historical fiction with interwoven timelines, archival mystery, and folkloric magical realism
positioning.description: Daughters of Babylon sits in the upmarket/literary space where historical fiction, contemporary literary mystery, and myth-inflected magical realism overlap. Its core engine is not plot-thriller momentum but a braided, poetically driven investigation: a grieving contemporary executor untangling a literary estate; a legendary medieval queen negotiating captivity, desire, and political peril; and a 1970s Veracruz nagual navigating ritual duty and prophetic threat. The book’s market position is strengthened by embedded poetry/archives, multilingual/cross-cultural texture, and a sensory, lyrical voice—aimed at readers who value atmosphere, thematic depth (memory, legacy, agency), and intertextual resonance across time.

moodAndTone.title: Mood & Tone
moodAndTone.subtitle: Lyrical, elegiac, slightly uncanny—sensual, ritualistic, and intellectually curious
moodAndTone.description: The dominant mood is melancholic and contemplative, with a ritualistic undertow and intermittent tension from political danger, legal disputes, and supernatural threat. The tone is literary and sensory (synesthesia, coastal and claustrophobic spaces, manuscript tactility), frequently intimate and mythic, with dry humor as a counterpoint. Emotional movement trends from dislocation and grief toward curiosity and tentative renewal, while maintaining a bittersweet aftertaste. Romance and sensuality are present but largely implied, functioning as texture and character-pressure rather than explicit heat.

marketing.title: Daughters of Babylon: Lyrical Dual-Timeline Literary Historical Fiction Launch Plan
marketing.subtitle: A stage-1, globally-positioned strategy to sell a poetic archival mystery with mythic/magical elements to upmarket adult readers
marketing.objective: Drive qualified discovery and conversion for an upmarket literary historical novel by positioning it as a dual-timeline, archive-driven mystery with lyrical prose and folkloric magic, optimizing for preorders (if available), launch-week sales, and sustained book-club uptake.
marketing.keyInsight: Readers who buy upmarket literary historical fiction respond strongly to (1) a clean organizing hook (dual timelines + archive/found texts), (2) emotional stakes anchored in grief, desire, and agency, and (3) “smart” atmospherics (poetry, multilingual texture, myth/ritual) that create book-club talk value—making this title best marketed as a literary mystery with historical grandeur rather than as romance or high fantasy.
howToUse: Use the messaging framework to keep all assets consistent: archival mystery + lyrical atmosphere + cross-cultural myth/ritual + grief-to-renewal emotional arc.

Lead with the most legible hooks in ads and retailer copy (found manuscripts, walled-alive legend, ruined priory, queen in captivity), then deepen with poetry excerpts and sensory lines in owned channels.
Create two asset lanes: (A) “Mystery/Archive” creatives for broad reach and conversion, and (B) “Poetry/Lyrical” creatives for community building and high-intent readers.
Prioritize book-club discoverability early: discussion guide, book-club pitch email, and outreach to organizers before heavy paid spend.
Localize only lightly for global audiences: keep US English copy, but rotate geo-targeting and retailer links by region (US/CA/UK/AU/NZ where applicable).
Track weekly KPI movement, refresh creatives every 10–14 days, and roll winning hooks into back-cover copy, A+ content, and author/press pages.
primaryKPIs: Amazon/retailer page conversion rate (detail page views to purchase)
Email list growth (net new subscribers) and welcome-series open/click rates

funnels.name: Awareness
funnels.description: Introduce the premise and mood: a queen in captivity, a nagual in 1972 Veracruz, and a contemporary executor unraveling a poetic legacy—linked by ritual, desire, and archives across time.
funnels.formats: 15–30s mood trailer video, quote cards (poetry/sensory lines), carousel “3 timelines / 1 mystery,” author/press interviews, podcast guesting, festival and panel appearances
funnels.optimisation: Optimize for video views and engaged reach; test 3–5 hooks (walled-alive legend, found manuscripts, Eleanor captivity, Veracruz nagual, ruined priory). Retarget 50%+ viewers and engagers into consideration.

funnels.name: Consideration
funnels.description: Build intent with proof and specificity: comps, themes (grief, memory, agency), archival artifacts, and the book-club angle; reduce “literary risk” by clarifying what kind of read it is.
funnels.formats: Landing page with sample chapter + discussion guide, excerpt audio, newsletter sequence, Goodreads giveaway (where available), long-form podcast interviews, Bookstagram/BookTok creator reads, blog posts on Eleanor/poetry/ritual research
funnels.optimisation: Optimize for landing page views, email sign-ups, and clicks to retailer/indie links; retarget site visitors and engaged video viewers with excerpt and review snippets.

funnels.name: Conversion
funnels.description: Capture high-intent readers with clear CTAs to buy/borrow; focus on retailer optimization, book-club bundles, and event-driven spikes.
funnels.formats: Retargeting ads (purchase objective), retailer deal callouts (where available), signed-copy/indie incentives, virtual launch + readings, library ordering assets, paid newsletter placements (BookBub/Genre newsletters where fit)
funnels.optimisation: Optimize to purchases/clicks with tight creative rotation, strong CTA, and region-specific links. Use social proof (early reviews, blurbs, award/longlist mentions if obtained).

budgetAllocation.title: Stage-1 Budget Allocation (Percent Split)
budgetAllocation.breakdown: Paid Social (Meta/IG): 35% (primary testing + retargeting). Creator/Influencer seeding: 15% (Bookstagram, literary TikTok, poetry creators). Newsletter swaps/paid email placements: 15% (BookBub where eligible, literary newsletters). Events & festival support: 15% (virtual + select in-person). PR & podcast support tools: 10% (press kit, pitching support, transcription/clips). Creative production: 10% (trailers, quote cards, landing page design).

flightSchedule.title: 12-Week Stage-1 Flight Schedule
flightSchedule.timeline: Weeks -6 to -4 (Foundation): metadata polish, retailer copy/A+ content, landing page, discussion guide, ARC outreach, creator seeding list. Weeks -4 to -2 (Awareness ramp): launch trailer + hook testing, podcast pitching, excerpt drops. Weeks -2 to Launch Week (Intent building): retargeting begins, Goodreads pushes, email sequence, indie/library outreach. Launch Week (Conversion peak): daily short-form clips, live event/reading, strongest ad set scaled, PR beats. Weeks +1 to +6 (Sustain): book-club programming, themed content (Eleanor/Veracruz/priory), continued retargeting, festival panels, refresh creatives every 10–14 days.

lookaalikeAudiences.refreshCadence: Every 14 days during launch window; monthly thereafter, or immediately after major list growth spikes.
prioritisationRules: Prioritize LALs built from discussion guide downloads and sample-chapter views over general engagers.
Use 1% LAL for conversion and retargeting expansion; use 2–3% for consideration; use 4–6% only after ROAS/CPA stabilizes.
Do not scale budgets on a creative until it has stable CTR and post-click engagement for 5–7 days.

messagingFramework.title: Positioning + Message Pillars
messagingFramework.primaryTagline: A queen in captivity. A poet’s legacy in ruins. A spell of memory stretching across centuries.
supportingMessages: An upmarket dual-timeline novel blending medieval court intrigue, 1972 Veracruz ritual life, and contemporary archival discovery in southern France.
A grief-driven literary mystery: when a mentor dies, her executor finds poems, journals, and a trail that refuses to stay in the past.
Lyrical, sensual, and slightly uncanny—where translation, ritual, and desire shape what survives.
For readers who love found manuscripts, layered histories, and mythic realism that deepens (rather than replaces) emotional truth.

romanceReaders.title: For Romance-Adjacent Readers (Low-Heat, High-Feeling)
romanceReaders.message: This is a sensual, emotionally intimate novel where desire and devotion matter—but the engine is mystery, legacy, and voice. If you like slow-burn connection threaded through high-stakes personal choices, you’ll find ache and tenderness here without explicit heat.

bookClubs.title: For Book Clubs
bookClubs.message: A discussion-rich read about what we inherit, what we translate, and what we hide to survive—spanning Eleanor of Aquitaine’s captivity, a Veracruz nagual’s visions, and a contemporary woman sorting a mentor’s estate. Big themes, braided timelines, and plenty to debate about art, ethics, and memory.

matureReaders.title: For Mature Readers
matureReaders.message: A reflective, elegantly written story about grief, legacy, and the long tail of history—atmospheric rather than frenetic, emotionally resonant rather than plot-only, with the depth and texture of lived experience.

ruralReaders.title: For Rural/Small-Town Readers (Place-Based Appeal)
ruralReaders.message: From a coastal fortress and a village in Veracruz to a secluded priory in southern France, the novel treats place as a living force—where community ties, tradition, and survival shape what people can say aloud.

sampleCopy.title: Ready-to-Use Copy Toolkit
sampleCopy.backCoverBlurb:
When Silvina is named executor of her mentor Vivian Lansdowne’s estate, she expects paperwork, not prophecy. In a house crowded with journals, poems, and brittle artifacts, Silvina begins to sense a story that doesn’t belong to one lifetime—or one language.

Centuries earlier, Eleanor of Aquitaine watches the sea from captivity, her world narrowed to stone, politics, and a fierce resolve to preserve what cannot be governed: desire, verse, and the names that history tries to erase. In 1972 Veracruz, Lupo Sánchez—a nagual bound to ritual duty—moves through visions that feel less like dreams than messages meant to be carried.

As Silvina follows Vivian’s trail to a ruined priory in southern France, the past gathers like weather: manuscripts surface, legends sharpen, and the boundary between scholarship and the uncanny thins. Daughters of Babylon is a lyrical, interwoven novel of grief and inheritance—where poems become evidence, rituals become maps, and what was buried insists on being read.

socialMediaPosts.text: A mentor dies. A house of journals and poems is left behind. And an executor begins to suspect the past is not finished speaking. #DaughtersOfBabylon #LiteraryFiction #HistoricalFiction
Eleanor of Aquitaine in captivity—stone walls, court politics, and the stubborn need to preserve a voice. A story where poetry becomes survival.
Veracruz, 1972: a nagual walks the line between family and ritual, carrying visions that won’t let him look away. Magical realism with teeth—and tenderness.
Found manuscripts. A ruined priory. A legend of a woman walled alive. If you love archival mysteries braided with history and myth, this one’s for you.
This book begs to be heard: lyrical prose, interwoven timelines, and poems that echo across centuries. Audio readers—put it on your list.

videoCreativeScripts.script:
VO (calm, intimate): “A woman inherits a poet’s papers… and finds a story that doesn’t belong to one century.”
On-screen text: THREE TIMELINES. ONE LEGACY.
Cut: Rain on a stone window. A crown-shaped shadow. A hand smoothing a manuscript page.
VO: “Eleanor of Aquitaine—confined. A nagual in Veracruz—called by ritual. A modern executor—pulled into an archive that feels alive.”
On-screen text: POETRY. RITUAL. MYSTERY.
VO: “What was hidden to survive… insists on being read.”
End card: Daughters of Babylon + author name + “Read a sample / Order now”.
videoCreativeScripts.soraPrompt: Create a 25-second cinematic book trailer with lyrical, atmospheric visuals. Scenes: (1) medieval stone turret window with rain streaks overlooking a grey sea; (2) close-up of an illuminated manuscript and a modern typed page taped to a wall; (3) moonlit cave in Veracruz with stalactites and a gourd on the ground; (4) ruined French priory at dusk with wind moving tall grass. Color palette: deep indigo, parchment gold, sea-grey. Camera: slow push-ins, shallow depth of field. No readable text on pages. Add subtle drifting dust motes and candlelight flicker. Tone: contemplative, uncanny, elegant.

videoCreativeScripts.script:
On-screen text: FOUND POEMS. FOUND TRUTHS.
VO: “She thought she was settling an estate.”
Cut: Keys on a desk; a folder labeled “Vivian”; a map of southern France.
VO: “Instead she opened a door—into a queen’s captivity, a ritualist’s visions, and a legacy written in more than one language.”
On-screen text: DUAL TIMELINES • LITERARY MYSTERY • MAGICAL REALISM
End card: “Download the discussion guide.”
videoCreativeScripts.soraPrompt: Create a 20-second modern literary mystery trailer. Visuals: desk with old keys, archival folders, scattered photographs, a French map with hand-drawn circles, candlelit close-ups of handwritten notes, and a brief flash of a medieval corridor. Lighting: warm practical lamps with soft shadows. Style: upscale, minimal, museum-like. Motion: slow pans and match cuts between past and present. No gore, no explicit content.
